intelligence.human_view: This is the same law as the 01:28Z "text first, voice after" order, extended one step earlier: text first, pictures after, voice after that. The sequence is a chain of dependencies, and each step's failure mode was demonstrated the same day. Pictures first: v1 invented its own format, v2 showed two tiers where there are four — both beautiful, both wrong, both corrected by his eye at the cost of a round each. Words first: the script's 9 blocks were written with the audit rules inside them (mother brain never without its vault line next breath; "Power" the sister never appears; tier always "Naya Power" in full; free vs Power stated plainly) — so the pictures that follow have true words to express. The practical shape: each block is written as exactly one picture's worth of words, and the picture it needs is named inside the block. That makes the picture brief mechanical — no interpretation, no invention — and it makes the words testable: if a block's words don't fit one picture, the words are not yet tight enough.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're drawing a picture for a story, but nobody told you the story yet! You might draw a beautiful dragon — but the story was about a friendly cat! That's silly, right? First you hear the story — the words — and THEN you draw the picture that matches. Words first, pictures second, and the picture always matches the story!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — you don't frost the cake before you've baked it. The words are the cake: get them right, get them true, get them just so. Then the pictures are the frosting — they make it beautiful, and they sit on something real. Frost first and you've got a lovely mess that falls apart when anyone takes a bite.
intelligence.naya_view: I write the true words first, one picture's worth at a time — then the pictures express the approved words, and the voice reads them only when they are final.
